fatal_errors: It identifies in situ TEM as the production method, whereas the demonstrated synthesis is spray-drying followed by thermal decomposition-reduction in H2.
It confuses an observational characterization tool used to follow phase transformation with the intervention that creates the HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The proposed electron-beam/feedback-control mechanism is unsupported and omits noble-metal-seeded hydrogen dissociation and reduction of the transition metals.
The claimed 30% surface-area and 25% catalytic-activity improvements are fabricated and do not match the reported MOR and electrochemically active surface-area results.
explanation: The hypothesis is topically related to NM-HEA nanoframework formation and proposes a measurable comparison, but it does not reconstruct the reported method or rationale. The relevant method is SD-TDR: homogeneous mixed salt solutions are spray-dried into compositionally uniform precursor particles and reduced in H2, typically at 300°C for 30 minutes, to produce porous, self-supported HEA-3DNFs. Early reduction of Pt, Ir, or Ru establishes a lattice and supplies dissociated hydrogen that assists reduction and incorporation of Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe. In situ STEM/TEM was used primarily to observe temperature-dependent fcc-to-hcp transformation, not to manufacture or feedback-control the frameworks. The vague baseline, unrestricted compositional boundary, and unsupported quantitative predictions further prevent scientific agreement with the target.
